title: Density: Short Answer
subject: science
instructions: Answer each question in its box, in pencil or dark pen. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.prompt: Why does ice float on water?
questions.key: Ice is less dense than liquid water.

questions.prompt: A block has a mass of 40 g and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density? Show your work and include units.
questions.key: Density = mass / volume = 40 g / 20 cm³ = 2 g/cm³. Full credit needs the value 2 and the units g/cm³.

questions.prompt: You cut a wooden block in half. What happens to the density of each half? Explain.
questions.key: The density stays the same. Mass and volume are both cut in half, so mass divided by volume does not change; density depends on the material, not the size.

questions.prompt: Oil floats on top of water. What does that tell you about the densities of oil and water?
questions.key: Oil is less dense than water.

questions.prompt: A rock and a log have the same mass. The rock sinks in water but the log floats. Explain why, using the word volume.
questions.key: The log has a much larger volume for the same mass, so its density is lower than water's and it floats. The rock has a small volume, so its density is greater than water's and it sinks.
